newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse ends profit-taking cycle - brokers.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse ends profit-taking cycle - brokers.

text.p: Moroccan stock market closed higher on Thursday, but stockbrokers said it ended the profit-taking cycle by some investors, stockbrokers said.
The all-share index rose 0.54 percent to close 429.60 points compared with the previous session.
In recent weeks, the bourse index went beyond 400 points, due mainly to heavy trading of blue chip companies.
"The profit-taking cycle was halted by a regain of interest by the local mutual funds who were collecting an average of 30 million dirhams a week,: a Moroccan market analyst said.
Societe Nationale d'Investissment, one of the market's largest capitalisations, continued its upward trend to close at 605 dirhams, up four dirhams on the previous session.
ONA Group, Morocco's largest conglomerate, dropped five dirhams to close at 445 dirhams.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market's liquid stocks, gained again four dirhams to close at 412 dirhams.
Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the market's largest bank, which made significant gains in recent weeks, was not traded.
The bourse traded volume was 48.5 million dirhams, up from 28.4 million dirhams. ($1= 8.7 dirhams)
